name: WV-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+20 partisan lean makes it deeply Republican territory
Incumbent Riley Moore holds a roughly five-to-one fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 97 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; Ace Parsi has limited resources
model.rationale: An R+20 district, a well-funded incumbent, and market pricing near 97 percent Republican leave almost no path for Ace Parsi; even a favorable national environment for Democrats only trims the expected margin.
model.watch: A large influx of outside spending for Parsi or a dramatic national wave against Republicans could narrow the margin, though the seat would still be favored to stay Republican.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
West Virginia's Second District is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and incumbent Riley Moore returns as the clear favorite. He has raised about $1.56 million and holds more than $800,000 on hand, while Democratic challenger Ace Parsi has raised roughly $277,000 with under $100,000 available. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets price Moore's chances near 97 percent.

The fundamentals point the same direction: the district's twenty-point Republican lean, Moore's incumbency advantage, and his financial edge outweigh what appears to be a modestly favorable national environment for Democrats. Parsi would need a dramatic shift in the political climate or a large influx of outside money to make this competitive. Moore is expected to win by a wide margin, with the seat remaining safely in Republican hands.
